The production immerses guests in the history, legends, and living traditions of Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Through a seamless blend of mele (song), hula (dance), and oli (chant), alongside vibrant Polynesian performance traditions, Maui Nui Lūʻau guides audiences on a journey across the Hawaiian Islands and into the greater South Pacific. Live music, engaging narration, and dynamic choreography bring ancestral stories to life, balancing cultural authenticity with polished theatrical presentation.  
  
Complementing the performance is a curated island feast featuring traditional Hawaiian cuisine alongside contemporary island flavors. Guests enjoy staples such as kalua pua‘a prepared in an imu, fresh island fish, lomi lomi salmon, poi, tropical fruits, and locally inspired desserts. The culinary program reflects both heritage and hospitality — offering abundance while honoring time-honored preparation methods and the communal spirit central to the lūʻau tradition.  
  
As one of West Maui’s recognized lūʻau experiences, Maui Nui Lūʻau maintains a reputation for consistent performance excellence, professional production standards, and thoughtful cultural stewardship. Through music, dance, storytelling, and shared meal, the experience invites guests to connect not only with the beauty of Kā‘anapali’s shoreline, but with the enduring spirit and legacy of Maui Nui itself.

Whoa Dea Ranch offers guided coastal horseback riding tours on Kauaʻi’s west side near Waimea. Our small-group rides are limited to a maximum of 5 guests per tour, creating a more personal horseback riding experience through open coastal landscapes with sweeping Pacific Ocean views, access to a private black sand beach, and a memorable stop near the historic pier.  
  
First-time and experienced riders are welcome. Tour options include the Early Bird Saddle Up, Coastal Morning Saddle Up, Sunset Saddle Up, and a Private Saddle Up Ride for up to two guests. Guests are thoughtfully matched with our well-cared-for horses, and our guides focus on safety, comfort, and an enjoyable riding experience.  
  
Our standard horseback riding tours are available for riders ages 10–72. For couples looking for a romantic activity on Kauaʻi, our sunset and private horseback rides offer a memorable experience for anniversaries, honeymoons, proposals, birthdays, and other special occasions.  
  
Located on Kauaʻi’s west side near Waimea, Whoa Dea Ranch pairs especially well with a visit to Waimea Canyon and Kōkeʻe. Advance reservations are recommended. The official Whoa Dea Ranch website and direct booking source is WhoaDeaRanch.com.

title: North Shore Surf Girls
teaser:
North Shore Surf Girls Surf School invites you to experience the magic of surfing on Oʻahu’s legendary North Shore with a fun, safe, and truly local team. Based in Haleʻiwa and led by professional waterwomen and lifelong North Shore surfers, we specialize in unforgettable surf adventures for beginners, families, and returning wave riders alike.  
  
Our friendly, certified instructors provide personalized surf lessons at beautiful North Shore beaches such as Puaʻena Point and Chun’s Reef, chosen daily for the best waves and safest conditions. Whether it’s your very first wave or your next great ride, we make learning to surf easy, exciting, and rewarding.  
  
Beyond surf lessons, we also offer stand-up paddleboard tours on the scenic Anahulu River, group and family sessions, and custom experiences designed to help you connect with Hawaiʻi’s ocean lifestyle.  
  
As a locally owned North Shore business, we’re proud to share our love for the ocean, Hawaiian culture, and community. From reef-safe practices to warm island hospitality, every experience is guided by aloha, respect for the ocean, and a passion for creating lifelong memories.  
  
Come surf, paddle, and explore with us — and discover why the North Shore is the heart of Hawaiʻi’s surf culture

title: Hawaiian Music Perpetuation Society
teaser:
Lokomaikaʻi Hawaiʻi Heritage Center is a community-rooted cultural space dedicated to preserving and sharing the ʻike (knowledge) and values of Hawaiʻi’s past. It is not just curated by institutions, but by the community itself—guided by the wisdom of kūpuna (elders), cultural practitioners, and generational stories that ensure authenticity and continuity.  
  
The center weaves together historical artifacts, oral histories, and lived experiences, grounding its exhibits in ʻike passed down through time. Mele (songs and chants) play a central role, serving as both historical record and spiritual guide—carrying lessons, place-based knowledge, and ʻike that inform how the community moves forward.  
  
In this way, the center becomes a living archive—where the voices of the past actively shape the future through culture, memory, and shared kuleana.

title: Komohana Charters
teaser:
Komohana Charters is a locally owned and operated family boat charter company on the Island of Kaua‘i. We specialize in exclusive private and small group shared NaPali Coast boat tours. Operating year round out of Kikiaola Small Boat Harbor on the westside of the island.  
  
Our catamarans provide a comfortable, customizable alternative to larger commercial tours. From snorkeling and whale watching to sea cave exploration and custom adventures like fishing, every trip is built around your group and the experience you want to create. Because of our smaller size, we’re able to access areas and sea caves that many larger boats simply can’t.  
  
When envisioning the experience we wanted to share we came up with phrase “Make your own waves” as we believe that the best memories are made away from crowds, through genuine local hospitality, adventure, and experiences made for you and the people closest to you.

title: Henry Kapono Foundation
teaser: Founded in 2018 as a 501(c)(3) organization, the Henry Kapono Foundation (HKF) is rooted in Hawai‘i and driven by the vision of celebrated entertainer Henry Kapono and his wife, Lezlee Kaʻaihue. Guided by Henry’s lifelong passion for music and his love for the islands, HKF is dedicated to giving back to the community that has shaped his life. By empowering creators to develop, share, and amplify their talents, HKF fosters collaboration, mentorship, and the choice to build meaningful careers, here at home, or abroad.HKF’s ultimate goal is to elevate Hawai‘i’s music to its fullest potential—celebrating its authentic, vibrant, and diverse culture while establishing it as a globally recognized, world-class music destination.

title: Hawaii Glass Bottom Boats
teaser:
Hawaiʻi Glass Bottom Boats is a locally owned and operated tour company offering unforgettable ocean experiences along the world-famous Waikīkī coastline. Our U.S. Coast Guard-inspected vessels provide guests with a unique opportunity to explore Hawaiʻi's marine environment through panoramic glass-bottom viewing windows while enjoying the beauty of the Pacific Ocean.  
Our experiences include wildlife and reef tours, scenic coastal cruises, sunset cruises, seasonal whale watching, Friday night fireworks cruises, and private charters. Every tour is led by experienced, safety-focused captains and crew who are passionate about sharing Hawaiʻi's incredible ocean, marine life, and aloha spirit with visitors from around the world.  
  
We are committed to providing exceptional customer service, creating memorable experiences for families, couples, groups, and visitors of all ages. Complimentary water and juice are provided on every cruise, and guests are welcome to bring their own food and beverages, making each tour a comfortable and personalized experience.  
  
As a locally owned small business, we take pride in supporting Hawaiʻi's visitor industry while promoting responsible ocean stewardship, respect for marine wildlife, and sustainable tourism practices. Our mission is to provide a safe, educational, and unforgettable adventure that showcases the natural beauty of Oʻahu from both above and below the surface.  
  
Whether guests are visiting Hawaiʻi for the first time or returning to create new memories, Hawaiʻi Glass Bottom Boats offers one of Waikīkī's most unique and memorable ocean adventures.

title: Lyman Museum and Mission House
teaser: Located at 276 Haili Street in historic downtown Hilo, the Lyman Museum and Mission House tells the story of Hawai`i, its islands, and its people. Built in 1839, the Lyman Mission House is the oldest wood frame building on the Big Island, and is adjacent to the island's only Hawaiian history museum. Daily guided tours of the historic home are included with Museum Admission; call ahead for scheduling. The nationally-accredited and Smithsonian-affiliated Lyman Museum contains natural history exhibits on volcanoes and Big Island habitats as well as one of the top mineral and gem collections in the U.S. Learn about Hawai`i’s cultural history from exhibits on Hawaiian artifacts and the primary ethnic groups to come work on sugar plantations during the 19th and 20th centuries. The Museum Shop, open to the public, offers a selection of various Hawaiian history books and gifts by local artisans. Visit www.lymanmuseum.org for further information and news about special exhibits.

title: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center
teaser:
Experience the most authentic Hawaiian luau on Oʻahu at the Polynesian Cultural Center’s Ali‘i Luau. Set against a backdrop of waterfalls, gardens and a lagoon, let us transport you to another time in Hawaii's history.  
  
Discover true Hawaiian hospitality at this entertaining feast, which begins with a fresh orchid lei welcome. The sounding of the pu, or conch, signals the Royal Court’s arrival adorned in the colors and clothing of ancient royalty, or Ali‘i. Guests are serenaded by with sounds of the ‘ukulele and melodic steel guitar, while hula dancers showcase the dances of both ancient and modern Hawaii. It’s a feast fit for a king with traditional Hawaiian foods like Kalua Pork, a specialty prepared in a traditional underground oven.   
  
Some of our more popular packages:  
  
Ambassador Luau package - Available starting at $144.95 (includes a guided tour through our island villages, Ali'i Luau buffet/show, & evening show Ha: Breath of Life)  
  
Ali‘i Luau package - Available starting at $119.95 (includes admission to our island villages, Ali'i Luau buffet/show, and evening show Ha: Breath of Life)  
  
  
The Polynesian Cultural Center is open Monday through Saturday from 11:00am - 9:30pm. Closed Wednesdays and Sundays.   
  
For reservations or for more information, visit www.Polynesia.com or call us at 800-367-7060.

title: Ko Olina Resort
teaser:
Ko Olina encompasses 642 acres with sweeping ocean and mountain views and a string of jewel-like lagoons connected by more than a mile and a half of seaside pathways. The resort is edged to the north by the pristine nature preserve of Lanikuhonua (“where heaven meets the earth”) and to the south by four lovely beach coves.  
  
Ko Olina continues to set new standards for luxury vacation resorts with its mix of like-minded resort partners that include Aulani, a Disney Resort & Spa; Four Seasons Resort Oahu at Ko Olina; Marriott’s Ko Olina Beach Club; and the Beach Villas at Ko Olina.  
  
It is also home to the award-winning Ko Olina Golf Club and the Ko Olina Marina, Hawaii’s only private deep-draft marina.  
  
We aspire to be a role model for sustainable resort communities around the world. While it is a privilege to share Hawaii’s natural gifts, the ocean, aina (land) and sky, we are mindful of our responsibility to care for the environment we celebrate every day.  
  
Aloha. We invite you to find your own Place of Joy at Ko Olina.

title: Ocean Course at Hōkūala
teaser:

The Ocean Course winds its way through a mango and guava tree forest, down to the edge of the Pacific, with the finishing green in the midst of a 40-acre freshwater lagoon. title: Aikane Plantation Coffee Co.
teaser:
Aikane Plantation Coffee is 100% Hawaiian gourmet coffee, grown on our family estate located on the slopes of majestic Mauna Loa Mountain in the District of Ka’u.  
  
Our coffee is grown in fertile volcanic soil with just the right amount of Hawaiian sunshine.   
  
• We hand pick only the choicest cherries.  
• After the coffee cherries are pulped, the beans are high pressure washed to remove the mucilage.  
• The beans are then put into a vat with water to ferment over night.  
• The following morning they are pressure washed again to remove the fermentation.  
• After the beans are thoroughly washed they are placed on a screen to remove the excess water.  
• When dried to the touch, the beans are removed from the screens and placed on wooden drying racks where they are dried by the sun to our specific moisture content.  
• Next the beans are roasted to a Medium-Dark Roast and immediately placed in sealed foil bags.  
• To insure freshness, each bag has a one-way valve to keep freshness in and air out.

Whales and dolphins alongside the boat are just the beginning. Snorkeling in Hawaii means warm water, coral gardens, and neon-colored fish. Water play, waterfalls, lava fields, and talking story with locals—you’ve never lived aloha quite like this.  
  
Included highlights:  
\- Talk with a local Kahuna in Molokai’s ancient Halawa Valley  
\- Hike Hualalai Volcano—peer into the crater or venture inside a lava tube

title: Royal Kaanapali Course
teaser:
The Royal Ka'anapali Golf Course is the original resort course on Maui and features a unique Robert Trent Jones, Sr. design. Royal Ka'anapali opened with a tee shot from Bing Crosby in 1962 and hasn't missed a beat since. Ka’anapali Golf Courses has been home to PGA Tour events such as The Champions Skins Game, Golf Channel’s Big Break Ka’anapali, the original Shell's Wonderful World of Golf, the Canada Cup, and LPGA Kemper Open. Robert Trent Jones, Sr, took advantage of the rolling landscape to create gently sloping fairways and large contoured greens to ensure a challenging approach to each hole. Stretching 6,700 yards, this par 71 course will challenge your club selection and putting skills. The Royal Ka’anapali Course begins at sea level with a par 5 hole extending 550 yards. The course hugs the shoreline before winding its way to the West Maui Mountain foothills. Arnold Palmer called the 18th hole (par 4) one of the best and most challenging finishing holes he’d ever played.  
  
Experience Ka'anapali Golf Courses on Maui, Hawaii located in the heart of Ka’anapali Resort. Only steps away from the top beach in America, Ka’anapali offers 36 holes of premier championship golf, FootGolf and lessons from our PGA teaching professionals.  
  
The Golf & Resort Shop is open from sun up to sun down and shoppers have a variety of Ka'anapali logoed apparel to choose from be it for the beach, golf course or dinner out in the resort!

title: Wild Side Specialty Tours
teaser:
Into the Blue Connections - Step aboard a luxury power catamaran for an intimate, eco-certified journey into Hawaii’s wild blue backyard—home to 18 species of dolphins, 6 kinds of whales, and 5 types of sea turtles, all year round. Winter brings migrating humpbacks—breaching, singing, and nursing in the only U.S. breeding grounds—just miles from shore.  
  
Follow seabirds offshore to join playful spotted dolphins, elusive rough-toothed dolphins, or even the Hawaiian false killer whale. Nearshore, spinner dolphins leap while bottlenose pods charm. Along the way, snorkel Hawaii’s vibrant coral reefs—home to endemic fish, sleeping reef sharks, and turtle cleaning stations—guided by experts who know just where to look.  
  
Join the crew in hands-on citizen science: help photo-ID dolphins and whales, monitor reef health, and track marine debris. Your adventure supports real research and donates to local conservation.  
  
With shaded lounge space, a private restroom, and expert marine biologist guides, this is no ordinary tour—it’s an unforgettable, ethical encounter featured by National Geographic, Outside Magazine, Frommer’s and more.  
  
Comfort meets conservation. Discovery meets awe. Don’t just visit Hawaii—connect with it.

title: Maui Pineapple Tour
teaser:
Experience a Maui Pineapple like no other.  
  
Nothing is as synonymous with the Hawaiian landscape and culture as the pineapple. At Maui Pineapple Tour, our passion is to share the history, culture, and hard work that goes into producing this iconic fruit.  
  
Nestled in the tiny plantation town of Haliʻimaile in beautiful upcountry Maui, the tour begins in an air-conditioned vehicle that transports you into the pineapple fields. While traveling through the pineapple fields, knowledgeable guides explain the planting and harvesting techniques of the pineapple and show how plantation workers still cultivate the fruit by hand. Our pineapple was made famous by its extra sweet flavor and can’t be found anywhere else in the world. Nothing tastes sweeter than a hand-picked, machete-cut pineapple straight from the fields.  
  
After exploring the plantation, guests are guided through the processing factory and shown how pineapple is tested, sorted, and packaged. Everyone on tour receives a boxed Maui Gold pineapple as a take home gift. This pineapple can be easily taken through the airport for seamless travel back to the mainland U.S.  
  
Our Ohana is looking forward to sharing the history and culture of Maui Gold Pineapple with you!

Great champions and stories have emerged here, such as Greg Norman’s first win on America soil, Ian Woosnam and David Llwellyn’s thrilling victory for Wales in the World Cup of Golf and Morgan Pressel’s nail-biting win at the Kapalua LPGA classic. Two of the most popular PGA players ever, Fred Couples and Davis Love III, have each earned victories here - twice.  
  
The Bay Course is a championship course that is as challenging as it is beautiful. Known for its breathtaking 17th hole, the only hole to play over the ocean on Maui, it should certainly be on the "must play” list for any golfer visiting Maui.

Havaiki Nui (the great land beyond the horizon) beckons! We invite you to celebrate the spirit of adventure, romance and culture of these islands.

title: Tropics Bar and Grill
teaser: The popular beachfront cafe is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Featured on Hawaii Five-0 and many television shows, Tropics Bar and Grill is home to tropical exotic beverages, island inspired cuisine, and nightly entertainment.

title: Ha: Breath of Life at the Polynesian Cultural Center
teaser:
A story of passion ignited by fire, song, and dance. Ha: Breath of Life is a symbolic story of birth and death, love and family, triumph and tragedy, punctuated by Polynesian dance, music, and blazing fireknives. Told by a cast of over 100 young Polynesian performers, this emotional and energetic performance will truly take your breath away!  
  
The critically-acclaimed Ha: Breath of Life has attracted attention from around the world. Not only is it regarded as the #1 show in Hawaii, it has been described as, "Authentic pageantry teeming and throbbing with the syncopations and synergy of the south seas culture." - the Honolulu Star-Advertiser.  
  
Seating begins at 7p and the show begins promptly at 7:30p, ending at approximatetly at 8:45p.   
  
The Polynesian Cultural Center is open Monday through Saturday from 11:30a - 9p. Closed Wednesdays and Sundays.   
  
Packages begin at $89.95 and include entrance to our 6 island villages, dinner, and evening show.  
  
For reservations or more information, visit www.polynesia.com/ha-show or call 800-367-7060.

title: Aloha Mixed Plate
teaser: Oceanfront, outdoor restaurant and tropical bar featuring a menu of local favorites, noodles, burgers, and plate lunches. Catering also available. Fast and friendly tableside service in a relaxing atmosphere. Join us for lunch or dinner!

title: Princeville Condominiums
teaser: The resort town of Princeville sits atop bluffs overlooking the beautiful Pacific Ocean. Enjoy spectacular sunsets and views of Hanalei Bay and Bali Hai mountain. Golfers enjoy the challenge and fabulous views at the 27-hole Makai and 18-hole Prince courses. Although golf is a popular pastime, there are many other activities including sailing, fishing, kayaking, flightseeing tours and shopping. For a day in the sun, take a short, scenic drive to the beautiful white sand beaches of Hanalei Bay and Haena. During winter, watch for giant humpback whales and enjoy the antics of playful dolphins year-round. Outdoor lovers enjoy a day hike along the Kalalau Trail to Hanakapiai Beach and Falls, an informative tour of Limahuli Garden, a National Tropical Botanical Garden, or a leisurely kayaking adventure on Hanalei River. Watch the colorful skies of early evening on a sunset sail along the Na Pali Coast or reel in the big one on a sport fishing excursion.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: Oasis On The Beach
teaser:
Chef Zack Sato creates an array of delightful preparations featuring locally-grown, organic produce and fresh-caught island seafood.  
  
Located steps from beach, poolside at Outrigger Waipouli Beach Resort.

title: SpeediShuttle
teaser:
SpeediShuttle & Arthur's Limousines is the only transportation company offering statewide shared and exclusive shuttle, sedan, SUV, and limousine service, including traditional lei greetings at airport gates, on Maui, Oahu, Kauai, and Hawaii. Let us take you and your group to your destinations in our late-model, luxurious Mercedes-Benz and Lincoln fleet.  
  
All vehicles are fitted with GPS tracking and our Oahu Mercedes Shuttles offer FREE Wi-Fi for our guests. we can arrange ground transportation for groups from 2 to 25,000, no group is too large.

title: The Spa at Ko’a Kea
teaser: Located in the Ko‘a Kea Hotel & Resort, relax and renew in one of five luxurious treatment suites at The Spa at Ko‘a Kea.

title: Aston Kona by the Sea
teaser: Set on the west side of Hawaii Island, Aston Kona by the Sea is an oceanfront condo resort - an idyllic Hawaii retreat. The property offers gorgeous views of the Kona coastline, where guests can sunbathe and explore the tidepools. When venturing out, head to the charming town of Kailua-Kona, known for its eclectic shops, dining, and nightlife. The resort's location is also near many must-do activities and attractions including snorkeling, golfing, Kona coffee farms, and breweries. On-site amenities include a pool, sandy lounge area with barbecues, and event space available to rent for meetings and receptions. Guest suite accommodations each include full kitchens, private balconies, and WiFi access.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: Tidepools Restaurant
teaser: Dine Hawaiian-style. Feel the romance in thatched-roof bungalows that seemingly float above a koi filled lagoon at the base of a waterfall. Savor contemporary Hawaiian cuisine featuring fresh fish and steak in this extraordinary setting.

title: Aupaka Terrace
teaser: Start your day with a fresh cup of Kaua'i coffee, steaming latte, hot-from-the-oven breakfast pastry and other breakfast goodies at Kaua`i Marriott Resort's Aupaka Terrace.

title: Polo Beach Club
teaser:
This hidden gem bordering the Wailea Resort is noted for its prime Maui beachfront location on Polo Beach. A breathtaking, idyllic beach, where guests have exclusive access to splash at the ocean's edge or venture further out to challenge the surf.   
  
Resort amenities include a beachfront swimming pool with jet spa, barbecue grills and an herb garden.   
  
Enjoy the sights and sounds of the ocean waves from each two-bedroom, two-bath suite. Enter through a marbled entryway that leads to a sunken living room with magnificent ocean views. Each suite offers a fully-equipped kitchen, separate living/dining area, bedrooms with private and semi-private baths, personal washer/dryer and ocean view lanai.  
  
Self-parking, Wi-Fi internet, daily housekeeping, $155 in gift cards to Wailea restaurants and spas, and a Maika'i grocery discount card included.

Accommodations: Vacation Rentals
Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: Old Lahaina Lūʻau
teaser: When you step through the gates at the Old Lāhainā Lūʻau, you’re swept into a well-preserved epicenter of Hawaiian culture, storytelling, and feasting with a breathtaking ocean view. This isn’t just any Hawaiian Lūʻau, it’s the best one the islands have to offer. Join us for an evening that shares the Hawaiian culture through hospitality, food, and entertainment.

title: Mauna Kea Golf Course
teaser:
Since 1964, the award-winning Mauna Kea Golf Course has led the way in standards of course beauty and design, solidifying its place in history as one of the Hawaii's most scenic and favored courses. Avid golfers and guests of Mauna Kea Beach Hotel enjoy Robert Trent Jones, Sr.'s design and its updates and beautification by son Rees Jones.  
  
Guests of Mauna Kea Beach Hotel may take advantage of superior amenities including practice facilities that feature a driving range and putting green. Brush up on techniques with a private lesson or group clinic or elevate your game while enjoying epic views of the Kohala Coast's rolling waves from nearly every hole, including the course's famous over-the-ocean par 3 hole #3.   
  
Gather at Number 3 Restaurant and savor a tasty menu and refreshing beverages.  
  
During your Hawaii golf vacation, find value with our featured golf vacation packages; pairing rounds of golf with luxurious accommodations.

title: Royal Sonesta Kauaʻi Resort
teaser: Nestled on a quarter mile of white sand beach. Provides an irresistible combination of Hawaiian hospitality and luxurious accommodations. Housed amid 51 acres of lush exotic gardens, the resort is a short five-minute drive from the Lihue airport.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership
Pools: Largest single-level pool in the State of Hawaii

title: Ahaaina Luau
teaser: Waikiki’s only oceanfront dinner show is a culinary and sensory celebration, commemorating Hawaiian culture and transforming the traditional island experience in grand Royal Hawaiian style. The Royal Hawaiian’s ‘Aha‘aina is a lavish epicurean journey through time.

title: Hau Tree
teaser:
A Hawaii vacation doesn't take a lunch break-it's part of the fun and many pleasures of the Mauna Kea experience. Enjoy time out of the sunshine relaxing oceanside at Hau Tree restaurant. The menu includes delicious sandwiches, hamburgers, hot dogs, fries, island-fresh salads and ice cream treats including Mauna Kea's famous and refreshing Ovaltine Froth.   
  
And if there's ever been a better barstool for watching a perfect Pacific sunset, we don't know where it is. Hau Tree's Gazebo Bar on Kauna‘oa Bay is just about the best spot anywhere for a smooth tropical cocktail, and you have to try our signature drink, the Fredrico while trying to catch a glimpse of the elusive green flash.  
  
A longstanding tradition that's still the Big Island's most remarkable seafood buffet, the Mauna Kea Clambake at Hau Tree each Saturday evening is romantic al fresco dining just like you remember, beachside under the stars.

title: Myths of Maui Luau at the Royal Lahaina Resort
teaser: As the sun sets across famed Kaanapali Beach, beating drums and the call of a conch shell signal the start of Maui's most exciting and longest running Polynesian luau. Enjoy a stunning celebration of music and dance that culminates with an amazing fire knife finale sure to dazzle the entire family.

title: Ilima Terrace Restaurant
teaser: Asian, American, and Hawaiian dishes are offered, also lavish daily breakfast buffet, Lunch and Sunday Brunch.

title: OUTRIGGER Kona Resort & Spa
teaser: With decadent waterfront dining options, spacious island-inspired rooms with balconies, impressive oceanfront event spaces, and a host of on-site amenities and activities, OUTRIGGER Kona Resort and Spa makes it easy to experience one of Hawaiʻi's most storied locations. Snorkel, scuba, or swim Keauhou Bay, attend a dazzling and memorable luau, explore the legendary coffee farms of Kona, or discover the iconic volcanoes and nature reserves of the Big Island. Adventure awaits at OUTRIGGER Kona Resort and Spa.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: The Orchid Court
teaser: Start the day right with a delicious breakfast. The Orchid Court features offers bountiful traditional and island favorites at our daily breakfast buffet plus tempting a la carte items, fresh juices and exceptional service. Seating is available inside or outside overlooking the lawn, pool and ocean. Open daily.

title: Hau Tree Bar
teaser: Enjoy the spectacular view of Waikiki Beach and Diamond Head as you enjoy a tropical drink under the Hau Tree. Island inspired cuisine available throughout the day. Located Beachfront near Rainbow Tower.

title: Swim
teaser: Sip and savor your way at the poolside SWIM Restaurant and Bar overlooking Waikiki Beach. Enjoy live music and entertainment, nightly. Serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with local favorites and specialty beverages all days of the week.

title: Sheraton Maui Resort & Spa
teaser: One of Hawaii’s best resorts located on the best stretch of one of the world’s top beaches, Sheraton Maui Resort & Spa was named Best Hotel in Hawaii in USA Today’s 2023 10Best Reader’s Choice awards, while Kaanapali Beach was ranked No. 1 in the US and No. 10 in the world in TripAdvisor’s 2023 Traveler’s Choice Awards for Best Beaches. Nestled against historic Pu‘u Keka‘a, or Black Rock, the Sheraton Maui Resort & Spa is set amidst across 23 ocean-front acres on the best stretch of Ka‘anapali Beach. Over 80 percent of the 508 guest rooms feature an ocean view, and the resort is home to exquisite dining, exciting water sports, and a full service spa, The Spa at Black Rock. Experience our legendary lele kawa—cliff diving ritual—and other immersive Hawaiian experiences available on property.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: Lagoon Grill
teaser: This is the place to meet and watch our resident dolphins frolic in the lagoon below, as you enjoy a casual outdoor lunch. Choose from burgers, hot dogs, salads, sandwiches and tropical fruits. Stop by and enjoy one of our famous smoothies, or try one of our refreshing tropical cocktails while watching the sun set on the Pacific Ocean... all at Lagoon Grill!

title: Don The Beachcomber
teaser:
The open-air Don the Beachcomber signature restaurant located at the Royal Kona Resort features a prime setting right on the water's edge. Diners enjoy spectacular views of the sun setting over the Pacific while savoring succulent Pacific Fusion, Prime Rib and seafood specialties. Watch the culinary team prepare entrees in the Exhibition Show Kitchen. Open daily for breakfast, dinner hours vary seasonally.  
  
After dinner, head next door to Don's Mai Tai Bar and try an original Mai Tai or one of ten Mai Tai variations while listening to some of the Island's most scintillating live entertainment including Salsa, Jazz, R&B; and Hawaiian.

The relationship between Hawaiian culture and the universe is showcased through a colorful variety of displays and interactive exhibits.

title: Luana Lounge
teaser:
In Hawaiian, "Luana" may be explained as "to be at leisure, enjoy pleasant surroundings and associates, live in comfort and easy, enjoy oneself, relax ... be content."   
  
Enjoy a leisurely afternoon or evening here with your favorite tropical libation, nibble from a delectable pupu menu and relax in comfortable furnishes surrounded by local Big Island art and the glorious Kohala sunset near the main Lobby.  
  
Open daily from 4:00pm with last call at 11:00pm. Live Hawaiian music provided by a solo guitarist and entrancing hula dancer from 5:30 - 8:30 pm.

title: DUO
teaser: Open-air restaurant features lavish breakfast buffet and Pacific Rim dining daily.

title: The Edge of Waikiki
teaser: Located on Waikiki Beach serving delicious pupus and exotic cocktails with live Hawaiian music nightly.

title: Red Salt
teaser:
Red Salt’s diverse menu by acclaimed Executive Chef and Kauai native Noelani Planas celebrates fresh Hawaiian seafood and produce in a casual, yet sophisticated seaside atmosphere. Modern dinner cuisine including vanilla bean-seared mahi, ahi tartare, and the decadently layered Red Salt burger are served in a contemporary setting. Select nights, the Red Salt Lounge* is host to a sushi bar featuring the day’s freshest catch in innovative, isle-inspired rolls.  
  
During morning hours, Red Salt offers tropical takes on traditional breakfast dishes, such as lobster benedict and lemon-pineapple soufflé pancakes, recently featured by Food Network.  
  
*Lounge and sushi bar seating are not available for reservation and is first come, first served.

title: Kani Ka Pila Grille
teaser: Kani Ka Pila Grille, located pool-side at the newly renovated Outrigger Reef on the Beach, serves lunch, dinner and tropical drinks daily, but its real draw is the top-notch live entertainment by some of Hawaii’s greatest island musicians, hot new local talent and island artists of international renown. The restaurant’s combination of food, libation and real local music by artists of exceptional caliber is akin to match made in Hawaiian Slack Key heaven.

title: Waikoloa Beach Course
teaser:
Winding its way through ancient lava fields along the breathtaking Kohala coastline, Waikoloa’s Beach Course is, resort golf at its finest. The 6,566 yard, Par 70 Beach Course was designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr. and was literally carved from the lava flow along the picturesque Anaeho’omalu Bay. Immaculate greens are well-guarded by numerous strategically placed white sand bunkers, shimmering water features, but the ultimate Big Island golf experience may be the Beach Course’s 502-yard par 5 seventh—known throughout the islands as the most spectacular oceanfront par-five in Hawaii. Not only is it a challenging golf hole, its rocky point over the breakers is an awesome place to spot humpback whales and misty, distant views of other Hawaiian Islands.   
  
Open daily from 6:30 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.   
Rates:

Junior Guests: $50   
Nike Rental Clubs: $50

Lounge: Mai Grille by Chef Allen Hess

title: Waipouli Beach Resort & Spa Kauaʻi by OUTRIGGER
teaser: Waipouli Beach Resort & Spa Kauai by Outrigger rivals the best Kauai hotels for luxury accommodations and access to island attractions. These beautiful condos are superbly appointed with gourmet kitchens and extra-spacious baths. The resort’s central feature is a free-form swimming pool with flumed water slides and cascading waterfalls. The on-site day spa and tapas-style restaurant add to the resort’s relaxed and refined ambience. The location takes full advantage of its surroundings with a breezy beachfront for morning strolls, and Kapaʻa Shopping Village just steps away for casual dining and convenient shopping.

title: Anara Spa
teaser: Find an oasis within at Anara Spa where the open-air setting maximizes Kauai’s ideal climate and beauty. Here, traditional healing methods blend with island-fresh botanicals to refresh and renew. Treatments take place in thatched roof bungalow or rooms that each open to their own private garden. In this lavish setting, guests are pampered with skin softening body renewal treatments, relaxing massages, facials, manicures, pedicures, and much more. Facilities include steam and sauna rooms, outdoor lava rock showers, whirlpools and a float pod. The largest spa on Kauai, Anara also features an open-air fitness and yoga room, a meditation lounge, soaking pools and a fitness room with state-of-the-art cardio and weight machines. Anara delivers a truly unique Hawaiian spa experience. MAE#982

title: Na Hoola Spa
teaser: Waikīkī's original destination for wellness. Promoting health and wellness using Hawaiian culture healing and arts, take a journey and let your body and spirit refresh and rejuvenate. Indulge in this full-service spa with gorgeous views of Waikīkī beach. Facials, massages, body treatments, couples treatments, and wedding services available.

title: Hau Tree
teaser: Lovely scenery, pure fresh air, clear blue sea, superb Pacific Rim cuisine, and heavenly sunsets hung over the Pacific Ocean. Great food and wonderful staff here to service you daily.

title: The Mai Tai Bar – Kaanapali Beach
teaser: The Mai Tai Bar - Kaanapali Beach is located near the Sheraton Maui pool and just footsteps from the beach. Named for the famed Mai Tai Bar on Oahu, this bar offers a variety of specialty drinks and tasty grilled favorites. Join the friendly bartenders for a pleasant Maui afternoon.

title: Moa Moa Hawaiian Fish House
teaser:
Discover Moa Moa, a dining experience featuring upscale Pacific Island cuisine with an open-air setting and gorgeous ocean view.

5:30pm - 9:00pm  
Reservations are required through Opentable or by dialing "0" from your guestroom phone.

title: Anaina Hou Community Park
teaser: Anaina Hou Community Park is located on 15 acres in Kilauea on the beautiful north shore of Kauaʻi, and offers entertainment, recreation, educational programs, healthy community services, and is in the process of building the 24-Million dollar Kauaʻi Resilience Center featuring state-of-the-art disaster shelter and vocational training. Our campus is enhanced by the Porter Pavilion events complex, botanical miniature golf course, 17,000 sq. ft. playground, weekly Farmers’ Markets, and the very unique outdoor Sunset Lānai. We serve our community and visitors in a myriad of ways and serves as a wonderful place to create everlasting memories!

title: Umalu
teaser: 'Umalu, meaning “the shade cast by a cliff” in Hawaiian, offers guests a reprieve from the sun. Located on the pool deck of Hyatt Regency Maui with views of the Pacific Ocean, ‘Umalu is open for lunch and dinner. Choose from a variety of fresh salads and creative sandwiches throughout the day at our shaded restaurant or between the waterfalls at our Grotto Bar. Also dine with us as late as midnight with our new dinner menu full of mouthwatering entrees; including Hawaiian Ahi and Herb Crusted Prime Rib.

title: Ikena Landing
teaser: Begin each morning in the open-air setting of ‘Ikena Landing with a delectable breakfast buffet or, select from a menu of taste-tempting and healthy ala carte options including fresh juices by The Juicery and vibrant, nutritious smoothies.

title: Hilo Hawaiian Hotel, Trademark Collection by Wyndham
teaser:
Overlooking Hilo Bay, the oceanfront Hilo Hawaiian Hotel, Trademark Collection by Wyndham, embodies authentic Hawaiian charm and aloha spirit. Situated along the historic Banyan Drive, this classic hotel offers breathtaking views of the majestic Mauna Kea, Moku‘ula Island, Downtown Hilo, and Lili‘uokalani Gardens.  
  
For over fifty years, the resort has welcomed visitors and served as a central venue for community events and family gatherings. It boasts Hilo’s only steakhouse, the WSW Steakhouse Restaurant (Whisky. Steak. Wine.), which serves breakfast and dinner, along with the Wai‘oli Lounge, featuring shared plates, a full bar, and live music.

title: Iolani Palace
teaser:
Visit the beautifully restored state apartments, including the Blue Room, State Dining Room and Throne Room, where King Kalakaua and his sister and successor, Queen Liliuokalani, held lavish entertainments and conducted the diplomatic affairs of the kingdom. View the private living quarters of the royal family, and listen to the poignant story of Queen Liliuokalani’s imprisonment in an upstairs bedroom following the overthrow of the Hawaiian monarchy.   
  
Tour the Palace Galleries that showcase the royal crowns, diplomatic orders, and personal jewelry of the royal family. See re-creations of the Palace Kitchen, China Storage Room and Chamberlain’s Office located nearby.  
  
Guided and audio tours of Iolani Palace are available Tuesday through Saturday. Ticket cost to the museum is: Guided $20 - Adults, $5 - Children 5-12; Audio Tour $13 - Adults, $5 - Children 5-12; Galleries: $6 - Adult, $3 - Children 5-12. Childen under 5 are free and admitted to Galleries only.

title: Kapalua Villas Maui
teaser: The Kapalua Villas is located in the stunning 22,000-acre Kapalua Resort on Maui’s northwest coast and features upscale accommodations with a choice of beachfront, mountain-side or golf course locations. Spacious one- to three-bedroom condominiums are available with full kitchens, washers/dryers and air conditioning. Premium Gold Villas feature remodeled kitchens, refreshed entertaining and dining areas, and redesigned bedrooms and baths. Guests enjoy exceptional services at this resort, including a 24-hour reception center, full-service concierge, complimentary resort shuttle and 11 restaurants. Additional privileges afforded by a daily $25 per villa resort fee include in-villa high-speed Internet access, advance tee times and preferred rates at two world-class golf courses, golf academy, day use access to the luxurious Kapalua Spa, court time at the Kapalua Tennis Garden, and miles of hiking trails.

Accommodations: Hotels and Resorts, Condominiums, Vacation Ownership

title: Wailea Elua Village
teaser:
As the only resort fronting popular Ulua Beach, the Wailea Elua Village spans across the entire sandy beach and provide unobstructed access to snorkeling, diving and swimming. This upscale resort features low-rise bungalow-style condos on 24 acres of manicured lawns and gardens, along the scenic Wailea Coastal Walk.   
  
This private, gated resort features 2 swimming pools, jet spa, covered beachfront pavilion, fitness center, paddle tennis court and golf putting green; and caters to guests seeking a calm, relaxing vacation.   
  
Beautifully appointed 1-, 2- and 3-bedroom condos feature a separate living room, dining area, fully-equipped kitchen, private bedroom(s), spacious lanai with barbecue grill and en-suite washer/dryer. Select from oceanfront view, ocean view or garden view suites.  
  
Self-parking, Wi-Fi internet, daily housekeeping, $155 in gift cards to Wailea restaurants and spas, and a Maika'i grocery discount card included.

title: Hale Kai
teaser: The Ocean Bar is the perfect venue for a most refreshing tropical libation. Located next to the pool and just steps from the ocean, the ambience is unbeatable. Opt for a causal pupu, or try our signature cocktail, the Kohala Sunset, as you toast another beautiful Kohala sunset.

title: Ulana Terrace
teaser:
Mornings in Kapalua, Maui are both bright and indulgent at this breakfast-only restaurant overlooking the gardens, pool and ocean. The varied menu features traditional and local favorites.  
  
Open daily 6:30 AM - 10:00 AM

title: Hula Grill
teaser:
Experience the true flavors of Maui delivered daily by Local Fisherman and Farmers to our open-air kitchen and Barefoot Bar on the water’s edge in Ka’anapali.  
  
With local, line-caught fresh fish, Maui grown produce, & all-natural meats, you will experience Hawaii’s unique culinary and cultural melting pot crafted and served with the true spirit of aloha.

title: Surf Lanai
teaser: The Surf Lanai is an upscale outdoor beach side restaurant positioned alongside the pool providing al fresco breakfast and lunch service. Surf Lanai specializes in mainland classic dishes with tropical accents presented in a refreshing manner utilizing heirloom ingredients and artisan baked goods.

title: Kauai Beach Villas
teaser: Kauai Beach Villas is a deluxe, oceanfront resort surrounded by tropical gardens and freshwater lagoons. Enjoy sunrise at the beach and relax on the warm sand or stroll down the endless coastline to explore tidepools and watch humpback whales and dolphins offshore. Play tennis on one of four courts, have a barbeque at one of the outdoor grills, plan a gathering in a private room near the pool or simply lounge on the lanai of your spacious condo with panoramic vistas. Enjoy the adjacent Kauai Beach Resort and experience the amenities of a hotel and the comforts of home while staying at the Villas. Pamper yourself by spending a day at the spa or bask in the sun at one of the pools with a cool drink. Kauai Beach Villas is centrally located and a convenient distance to a variety of activities. Wailua Golf Course offers challenge plus spectacular ocean views. Kayak Wailua River to hidden waterfalls or take a riverboat tour to the Fern Grotto, one of Kauai's "natural wonders."

title: Tapa Bar
teaser: This open-air bar is perfect for cocktails, a delicious menu of smash burgers, pizza, salads and nightly contemporary music. Stop by to enjoy a beverage, watch a sports game or enjoy the music. Located in the Tapa Tower next to the Tapa Pool.

title: Lobby Lounge
teaser: Enjoy evening cocktails, pupus, and entertainment nightly with unforgettable sunsets and sweeping ocean views.

title: Queens' MarketPlace
teaser:
A family-friendly shopping center with a wide variety of tropical foliage and water features including koi ponds.

Consistently ranked as one of the top golf courses in Hawaii, playing The Plantation Course is sure to be on every golfer’s bucket list. Designed by Ben Crenshaw and Bill Coore, the course was designed on a grand scale in keeping with its location on the slopes of the West Maui Mountains and offers dramatic ocean views from virtually every hole. Its lengthy 7,411 yard par 73 layout challenges the pros but it’s wide fairways and generous greens make it very playable for the average golfer. With dramatic elevation changes, this course offers plenty of downhill tee shots. You’ll feel like one of the pros when - with the aid of the aggressive slope of the 18th fairway - you will enjoy hitting one of the longest drives of your life.  
  
The Plantation Course is the site of the PGA TOUR's Sentry Tournament of Champions each January featuring an elite field of previous year's PGA TOUR winners. The field has included golf greats such as Tiger Woods, Vijay Singh, Justin Leonard, Ernie Els, Davis Love III and many more. The course record is set at 62 and tied between K.J. Choi (2003), Graeme McDowell (2011), Chris Kirk (2015), Jason Day (2015) and Xander Schauffele in his final round in winning the 2019 Sentry Tournament of Champions.

title: Holo Holo Charters
teaser:
No trip to Hawaiʻi is complete without witnessing Kauaʻi's sacred Nāpali Coast. This stunning stretch of coastline was once home to thousands of people and is now protected as a Hawaiʻi State Park. Feel the power of her 4,000’ cliffs, sparkling waterfalls, rainbows, pristine beaches, sea caves, turquoise water, and emerald valleys. Learn the history and legends of this fascinating landscape, as we look for Hawaiian spinner dolphins, green sea turtles, and seasonally (December-April) humpback whales. Join us in the morning for an adventurous snorkeling and sailing tour or in the afternoon for a more romantic sunset dinner cruise.  
  
Or, kick it up a notch by saying YES to our company’s signature all-inclusive tour to the Nāpali-Niʻihau Super Tour. On this unforgettable seven-hour ocean adventure, you’ll experience all the glory of the Nāpali Coast and then cruise 17 miles across the Kaulakahi Channel to Lehua Crater Seabird Sanctuary and the mysterious “Forbidden Island” of Niʻihau. These deeper, more remote waters offer superior wildlife viewing and exceptional snorkeling conditions.   
  
Whichever tour you choose, you’re in good hands. Our company’s four catamarans were proudly built here on Kauaʻi and are meticulously maintained for maximum safety, comfort, style. With our local expertise and genuine aloha hospitality, we aim to give our guests a greater understanding and appreciation for Hawaii’s physical and cultural landscapes.   
  
Tours depart daily from Port Allen Marina Center. All tours include delicious food, a creative selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, complimentary snorkel gear, and reef-safe sunscreen. Visit us online at holoholocharters.com and give us a call at 808-335-0815; our friendly office staff members are happy to help you determine which of our five unique tours is the best tour for you!

title: Fair Wind
teaser:
For over 50 years, Fair Wind Cruises has been a leader in Kona snorkel tours along Hawai‘i Island’s spectacular Kona Coast. Family-owned and locally operated from Keauhou Bay, Fair Wind is best known for its award-winning Kealakekua Bay snorkel tour to the world-renowned Captain Cook Monument.  
  
Kealakekua Bay is a protected Marine Life Conservation District and one of the best snorkeling destinations in Hawai‘i. Its calm, clear waters and thriving coral reefs are home to tropical fish, sea turtles, and spinner dolphins. Fair Wind’s spacious, custom-built vessels are designed for comfort, stability, and easy water access — making this Big Island snorkel tour ideal for families, first-time snorkelers, and experienced ocean lovers alike.  
  
Safety, hospitality, and environmental stewardship have defined Fair Wind for generations. All tours are led by highly trained, lifeguard-certified crews who provide in-water assistance, reef education, and personalized care to ensure every guest feels confident and welcome.  
  
As long-time operators in Kealakekua Bay, Fair Wind is deeply committed to protecting Hawai‘i’s marine ecosystems. The company promotes responsible snorkeling practices, reef-safe sunscreen use, and sustainable operations designed to reduce environmental impact. Sharing the ocean comes with responsibility — and Fair Wind has built its reputation on caring for the very reefs that make these experiences so special.  
  
Families have trusted Fair Wind for decades, often returning year after year to snorkel the same vibrant waters they first explored as children. That legacy of trust, combined with a strong commitment to safety and environmental leadership, continues to set Fair Wind apart as one of the most established and respected snorkel tour companies on Hawai‘i Island.  
  
When you choose Fair Wind, you’re choosing more than a tour — you’re choosing a company dedicated to preserving the beauty of Kealakekua Bay for future generations.  
  
Fair Wind is recognized as the best snorkel cruise on the Big Island by Frommer's Travel Guide, West Hawai’i Today Reader's Poll, and the Hawai’i Journal "Best of Hawai’i" Poll.

title: Captain Andy's Sailing Adventures
teaser:
For more than 40 years, Capt Andy’s has been exploring Kauaʻi’s Nāpali Coast by sea.  
  
Founded on Kauaʻi in 1983, Capt Andy’s has spent decades getting to know this coastline from the water. Our trips range from relaxed sailing aboard custom 65-foot Star Class catamarans to small-group raft adventures that get closer to sea caves, waterfalls and the contours of the coast.  
  
Our catamaran experiences pair time on the water with snorkeling, a chef-prepared lunch and an open bar after snorkeling. Sunset sails trade the snorkel gear for dinner, drinks and an evening run along Nāpali. For travelers looking for a more adventurous day, our rafts offer a faster, closer-to-the-water experience, with select expeditions visiting Nuʻalolo Kai, a remote cultural and archaeological site accessible by permitted boat.  
  
No two days on the water are exactly alike. Nāpali is wild coastline, and our crews draw on years of local experience to make the most of the coast while treating the ocean and the places we visit with respect.  
  
Choose from snorkel sails, sunset dinner sails, rafting adventures and private charters, all built around the same thing we’ve been doing since 1983: showing people Nāpali from the perspective we know best.

title: Honolulu Museum of Art
teaser:
We invite you to an immersive experience of global art and culture through an Island perspective. A vital part of Hawai‘i's cultural landscape, the Honolulu Museum of Art (HoMA) is a unique gathering place where art, community and education converge in the heart of Honolulu. In addition to an internationally renowned permanent collection, the Museum houses innovative exhibitions, an art school, the city’s only art house theater, two cafés and a museum shop within two iconic buildings.   
  
Its collection of more than 55,000 works spans 5,000 years and includes art by Claude Monet, Vincent van Gogh, Georgia O’Keeffe, Lee Bontecou, Nick Cave, Kara Walker, and John Singer Sargent. HoMA is also the place to see the arts of Hawai‘i—traditional art, art about the islands, and contemporary art by Native Hawaiian and local artists.  
  
On Fridays the museum is open until 9pm—after exploring the galleries and selfie-ready outdoor courtyards (including a koi pond and tranquil fountain), visitors can enjoy live music, dinner in the HoMA Café, art activities and a film or art talk in the Doris Duke Theatre. It’s a great way to experience local life—you won’t want to miss it when visiting O‘ahu.  
  
Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday 10 am to 6 pm; Friday 10 am to 9 pm. $25 general admission; all youth 18 and under free. See our website for more details.

title: Blue Hawaiian Helicopters
teaser:
Founded in 1985, and honored by National Geographic as "Hawaii's premier helicopter tour company," Blue Hawaiian is also the only one that serves all of Hawaii—Oahu, Maui, Kauai, and the Big Island.   
  
Blue Hawaiian was the first in the industry to introduce the incredible EC130-B4 "Eco-Star," the world's first 21st-century touring helicopter. This phenomenal machine set a whole new standard in environmentally responsible air touring. It's significantly quieter and incorporates all the latest cutting-edge technologies, materials, systems, and avionics. Plus it offers incomparable passenger comfort, 23% more interior space, individual "First Class" seats, raised theatre-style platform in the rear, and far more cockpit glass for fantastic sweeping views. And now, Blue Hawaiian also owns the largest fleet of Eco-Star T2s, the latest and most advanced generation of Eco-Star.  
  
Blue Hawaiian continues to operate a select fleet of Eco-Stars—the industry standard in touring helicopters, all purchased new and meticulously maintained by Blue Hawaiian's FAA staff of top A&P; mechanics. This extraordinary team of professionals has been recognized every year since 1997 with the FAA’s ultimate accolade, the Certificate of Excellence – Diamond Award. No other helicopter tour company can match this record.  
  
And, every year since 1995, Blue Hawaiian has received the Six Star Diamond Award for Outstanding Quality and Service from the American Academy of Hospitality Sciences—the world’s only aerial tour company so honored.

All of Island Helicopters’ tours offer passengers a bird’s-eye-view of sites like the Waimea Canyon (Grand Canyon of the Pacific), the magical Na Pali Coast, numerous waterfalls and vistas, and Mt. Waialeale Crater (one of the wettest spots on earth). For customers on the Jurassic Landing, the flight also includes a 25-minute stop and short walk to Manawaiopuna Falls.

Built in 1848, Hānaiakamalama is listed on the State and National Historic Registries and houses a collection of Queen Emma’s belongings, antiques, furnishings and royal regalia. Today the Palace is a historic landmark, museum, and cultural site preserved by the Daughters of Hawaiʻi.

teaser:
See the Best of Kauai in Just 1 Day!  
  
-Explore the best sites on the north and east shores of Kauai

Sprinters

Scenic Beauty and Hawaiian Culture  
Our dynamic and entertaining tour guides pick you up at your hotel and show you a day’s worth of spectacular scenery and breathtaking beauty on Kauai’s North & East Shores. Learn about the history and culture of Kauai and enjoy a no-host lunch at one of the local restaurants. Wailua River Boat Cruise & Fern Grotto  
  
Board a spacious, open-air river boat for a two mile leisurely journey to the Fern Grotto where you’ll enjoy a short nature walk through the rain forest. The Fern Grotto is a geological wonder of Kauai where ferns grow upside down from the roof of the grotto. A natural amphitheater of lava rock and tropical vegetation is the perfect backdrop as you are serenaded and entertained by Hawaiian musicians and hula dancers. The Wailua River is Hawaii’s only navigable river and is also a popular place for water skiing, kayaking, canoeing and stand up paddling.  
  
Kauai’s North & East Shores  
On our Kauai tour see the best beaches, mountains, waterfalls and Heiau’s (sacred ancient Hawaiian sites) on Kauai’s east shore. Stop and view Sleeping Giant from Kapaa Town, the Wailua River, Fern Grotto, Poliahu Heiau, Hauola City of Refuge, Opaeka`a waterfalls, NaMolokama Waterfalls, Kealia Beach, Hanalei Bay, Hanalei Taro Fields, Anini Beach and the Northshore areas. Visit the Kilauea Lighthouse and Wildlife Refuge where you can see Layson Albatross, Boobies, Tropic Birds and Nene Geese (the Lighthouse is open Wednesday to Saturday). During the winter you may be able to see Humpback whales.

teaser:

McBryde Garden is a botanical ark for threatened and endangered plants of the tropics. Located in the verdant Lawai Valley, it is home to the world’s largest collection of native Hawaiian species outside the wild, and extensive plantings of palms, flowering trees, ornamentals, orchids, and other plants from tropical regions. The landscape is a combination of sprawling expanses and niches of plantings, bordering a meandering stream. The Conservation & Horticulture Center serves as an intensive care unit for endangered species. The garden is adjacent to NTBG's Allerton Garden. Garden vehicles bring visitors into these valley gardens from the Southshore Visitors Center in Poipu.  
  
Self-guided tours of McBryde Garden available daily. Other areas of this garden are offered on the guided combination tour, which includes part of the Allerton Garden as well.

title: Tiki's Grill & Bar
teaser:
Tiki's Grill & Bar is a locally owned, hip, casual, retro South Pacific-style restaurant featuring nightly entertainment, local contemporary musicians, and weekly hula dancers. Tiki's menu features tastes of the Islands with a balance of casual American dining and Pacific-Rim fare, and also has an affordable children's or Keiki menu with local and mainland favorites. Whether it's a sandwich and cold beer, fresh seafood and glass of wine, or a refreshing tropical drink such as the signature 1944 Mai Tai paired with a beautiful tropical sunset, Tiki's has something on the menu for everyone.  
  
Tiki's was started in 2002 by three friends from the University of Hawaii (UH Manoa) who wanted to open a restaurant where they could hang out and bring their friends and family. It's remained a place where locals can not only enjoy great food and views while "playing tourist" but is also a favorite spot for them to bring their out-of-town visitors who are looking for the quintessential Hawaiiana-tiki bar experience. Conveniently located in the Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel near the Honolulu Zoo, Tiki's is easily accessible from any location around Waikiki and Honolulu and offers elevator access to its 3rd-floor perch on the oceanfront side of the hotel. For guests who valet with the hotel, Tiki's validates for the first 3 hours free.  
  
Tiki's award-winning kitchen is helmed by Executive Chef Ronnie Nasuti. After a proven record of successful and distinguished accomplishments, Chef Ronnie chose to hang his hat at Tiki’s nearly a decade ago, steering the already-popular destination to a higher level of dining and excellence. Chef Ronnie believes in the farm-to-table movement by visiting farms and building strong bonds with local farmers such as Mari's Gardens, Kunia Country Farm, and Nalo Farms, that pioneered the local produce movement; in addition to bringing in fresh island produce and breads, Chef Ronnie orders 175 pounds of local grass-fed beef, venison from Maui Nui Venison, and 450 pounds of locally caught or raised fish and seafood such as Ahi and Mahi every week. His delicious signature items and dinner specials that fuse Hawaiian/Pacific Island with American cuisine are the result of his dedication to the craft and cooking with locally grown and raised food.   
  
A familiar face in Hawaii’s culinary scene, Chef Ronnie is a regular guest on Hawaii News Now's morning “Kitchen Creations” segment. He also represents Tiki’s at multiple charitable events each year including: the Hawaii Foodbank's Great Chefs Fight Hunger gala; Kick Start, a charity for underprivileged kids to compete in Karate competitions on the mainland; Cheer for Champions fundraiser benefitting the Special Olympics; Localicious with the Hawaii Agricultural Foundation (HAF); Dazzle for Central Union Preschool (CUPS); Empty Bowl Hawaii for Aloha Harvest; Mangoes at the Moana at the historic Moana Hotel; Webco Golf Tournament to benefit St. Louis High School; Executive Women International's (EWI) scholarship golf tournament; Flavors by the Bay for the Kamaʻāina Kids community service organization; events to benefit the University of Hawaii, the Waikiki Aquarium, the Hawaii Tourism and Lodging Association (HLTA) at the State Capitol, the Global Tourism Summit at the Hawaii Convention Center; and many more.   
  
Chef Ronnie is also passionate about sharing his love for the culinary field with the next generation of professional local chefs, and supports the efforts and students of the Hawaii Culinary Education Foundation, the Culinary Institute of the Pacific, Leeward Culinary School, Palama Settlement, Pearl City High School and more through events and fundraisers.  
  
Tiki’s Grill & Bar is a premiere setting for any special group occasion. There are three unique private venue spaces within the restaurant and open-air bar lanai that have gorgeous views and a welcoming, vibrant atmosphere. Tiki’s is a wonderful location for any milestone occasion, from a wedding reception dinner to a welcome party meet-and-greet, corporate event or buyout, birthday, anniversary, graduation, or any other group event. Chef Ronnie's signature private buffet menus offer the same delicious mix of local and mainland favorites to please any palate. The full-service events, catering, and bar staff provide a stress-free, seamless experience from planning to execution.

title: Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site and Archives
teaser:
DISCOVERY: In three historic buildings guests can see and feel the dramatic changes the New England Missionaries brought to Hawaii starting in 1820.  
  
Visitors discover how a small group of New England missionaries – who came to the islands in 1820 – worked with the Native Hawaiians to introduce Christianity, to develop a written language, public education, western medicine and representative government.  
  
Tours at 11:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 1:00 p.m., 2:00 p.m., and last tour at 3:00 p.m. Tuesday – Saturday. General Admission $10, Seniors, Military, Kama‘aina $8, Students (6-college) $6.   
  
Visit us at www.missionhouses.org

title: Ali'i Kula Lavender
teaser:
In the Upcountry region of Maui, nestled on the slopes of Haleakala (House of the Sun), is the mystical Ali`i Kula Lavender farm.  
  
Relaxation, Rejuvenation and Renewal are all held in this magical place that the spirit calls home!  
  
Created by Agricultural Artist and Horticultural Master, Ali’i Chang, AKL’s 13.5-acre farm resides at an elevation of roughly 4000 ft. and is home to approximately 55,000 lavender plants and 20 different varieties of lavender. Lavender is a summer bloomer, however the farm grows about 9 varieties of lavender, that bloom all year round. Olive trees, hydrangea, Protea, succulents and an exceptional variety of other plants can be found on the farm, which offers the first and only Lavender Lifestyle experience on Maui.  
  
Ali’i Kula Lavender (AKL) is the premier purveyor of Sustainable Aloha through educational stewardship and nurturing the well being of our communities and planet for future generations. AKL produces products that enrich the quality of life by evoking joy, rejuvenation, comfort and serenity. Each product is carefully made using natural, botanical and organic ingredients as often as possible. As a lifestyle company, we are animal and earth friendly and encourage our visitors and guests to do the same. AKL hopes to play an integral role in supporting sustainable economies through agri-tourism and support our community based business model through agricultural education.  
  
Built on a value-centered philosophy of “Aloha” which means love, friendship and responsibility, AKL’s founding principle speaks to the quality of our relationships with the land, the community and each other. Aloha is what influences our behavior and encompasses our level of excellence and service we hope to provide. As stewards of the land, AKL promotes the best practices that respect the Earth and the Environment and gives special homage and respect to our Kupuna (elders) whose spirit has empowered us to nurture and protect our land and our people.
